annotations.text:
ONE HUE THROUGH THE WHOLE NEUTRAL RAMP

The first pass had cool inks (blue-leaning greys) over warm papers. That hue flip is what makes mid-greys look dirty. Every neutral now sits on hue 80 in OKLCH, from #26221C ink to #FBF8F4 paper — warm all the way down.

Three text greys, and all three clear 4.5:1 on all three grounds. The old #9AA0A7 I used for the ledger's "—" placeholders measured 2.57:1 and is gone.

FOUR SEMANTICS, ONE LIGHTNESS, ONE CHROMA

L 0.47, C 0.08, hue is the only variable: accent 200, positive 148, caution 75, attention 38. 0.08 is the highest chroma all four hues can actually hold in sRGB — above it two of them clip and the set stops being uniform, which is what happened in the first pass.

attention #814A39 is spent on STATE only: the row edge, the icon, the "Te laat" label. The reminder button went back to the accent — a routine action should never wear the alarm colour.

ICONS: ONE GRID, ONE OPTICAL WEIGHT

Every icon is drawn on a 20-unit box with round caps and joins. Stroke-width is scaled per render size so the painted line is 1.5px everywhere: 22px→1.36, 20px→1.5, 18px→1.67, 16px→1.88. The first pass mixed 1.6 through 2.0 at eight different sizes, which reads as ragged.

And the per-row padlocks are gone. Everything in the grootboek is posted, so a lock on every row said nothing. The marker column now carries exceptions only — here, the reversing entry.

TEN CLIENT COLOURS, HONESTLY MEASURED

L 0.55, C 0.07 — lighter and quieter than the semantics on purpose. Ten hues over a 300-degree arc with a 30-degree dead zone either side of the accent, so no client is ever mistaken for the UI's own colour (the old palette had a client literally equal to the accent).

The second strip on that artboard is the honest part: simulated deuteranopia collapses the ten to about five, and amber/lime become identical. Initials and name are load-bearing, not decoration.

Marker initials are pure #FFFFFF — the off-white paper tone only reaches 4.42:1 on the darkest client colour.
